claims.text: Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
Equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr undergoes rapid oxidation or pesting at high temperatures.
Approximately 4–5 at.% Cr should be introduced by substitution or overall compositional adjustment.
Adding approximately 4–5 at.% Cr will improve the oxygen resistance of equiatomic cast HfNbTaTiZr.
Cr addition will promote an adherent, continuous Cr2O3-rich surface scale.
Chromium has a strong oxygen affinity that drives its segregation to the alloy surface during high-temperature exposure.
Surface-segregated chromium preferentially oxidizes to form a dense Cr2O3 film.
The proposed Cr2O3-rich scale will act as a diffusion barrier and retard oxygen ingress.
The Cr modification will not disrupt the fine-grained BCC matrix claimed to be responsible for the alloy's ductility and yield strength.
A Cr addition near 4–5 at.% may produce a secondary Laves phase.
The Cr-modified alloy will have a significantly lower oxidation rate and mass gain than untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The Cr-modified alloy will have better oxide-scale integrity than untreated equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
The Cr-modified alloy will retain 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
The Cr-modified alloy will retain a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C.
The intervention is applicable to oxidation in ambient air at approximately 800–1000 °C for exposures up to 5 hours.
Mechanical performance should be preserved at room temperature and at 1000 °C under strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.

contradictions.description: The mechanism states that Cr will not disrupt the BCC matrix, while the uncertainty field acknowledges possible Cr-induced secondary Laves-phase formation. The cited related-alloy study specifically observed BCC plus Laves after adding 4.2 at.% Cr.
